_about: Grading rubrics for the open-ended prompts of Ques Sections 4-11. Each base prompt gets a content-calibrated difficulty (its angle variant is one level harder) and 5-6 key concepts. Phrases are lower-case substrings; matching any phrase credits the point. Used by the heuristic grader and passed to the LLM grader as the reference rubric.

s4.base: Explain the difference between a process and a thread.

rubric.label: Threads share the process's memory and resources

s4.base: Compare deadlock prevention, avoidance, detection, and recovery.

rubric.label: Avoidance with safe states / Banker's algorithm
Recovery by preemption, rollback or termination

s4.base: Explain paging, segmentation, and virtual memory.
Differentiate preemptive and non-preemptive CPU scheduling.

rubric.label: Preemptive: OS can interrupt a running process
Non-preemptive: runs until it blocks or finishes

s4.base: Explain normalization up to BCNF with a suitable example.

rubric.label: BCNF: every determinant is a candidate key

s4.base: Compare TCP and UDP and give practical use cases.
Explain compiler, assembler, linker, loader, and interpreter.

rubric.label: Compiler translates source to machine/object code
Assembler converts assembly to machine code
Linker combines object files and libraries
Loader places the program in memory

s4.base: Describe inheritance, polymorphism, abstraction, and encapsulation.

rubric.label: Encapsulation: bundle data and restrict access

s4.base: Explain race conditions and synchronization mechanisms.
Compare cache memory, RAM, ROM, and secondary storage.

rubric.label: Cache: fastest, smallest, near the CPU

s4.base: Explain indexing and its effect on database performance.
Describe the OSI and TCP/IP models.
Explain public, private, protected, and default access modifiers.

rubric.label: Protected: class, subclasses (and package in Java)

s4.base: Compare static binding and dynamic binding.

rubric.label: Static binding resolved at compile time

s4.base: Explain garbage collection and memory leaks.

s5.base: Write SQL to find the second-highest salary.

rubric.label: Uses MAX with a subquery or ORDER BY
Edge cases: fewer than two salaries, ties, NULL

s5.base: Write SQL to identify duplicate email addresses.

rubric.label: Returns the duplicate rows (join or window)

s5.base: Explain INNER JOIN, LEFT JOIN, RIGHT JOIN, and FULL JOIN.

rubric.label: INNER JOIN returns only matching rows
LEFT JOIN keeps all left rows
RIGHT JOIN keeps all right rows
FULL JOIN keeps rows from both sides

s5.base: Write SQL to find employees earning more than their department average.
Explain primary key, foreign key, candidate key, and composite key.

rubric.label: Primary key: unique, not null identifier
Candidate key: minimal unique key options

s5.base: Write SQL to return the top three salaries in each department.

rubric.label: Filters rank <= 3 in an outer query / CTE

s5.base: Explain WHERE, HAVING, GROUP BY, and ORDER BY.
Write SQL to find records present in one table but not another.

rubric.label: LEFT JOIN … WHERE right.key IS NULL
NOT IN and its NULL pitfall
Clustered index defines physical row order
Only one clustered index per table
Non-clustered index is a separate structure with pointers

s5.base: Write SQL to calculate a running total.

rubric.label: Transaction as a unit of work

s5.base: Write SQL to remove duplicate rows while retaining one record.

rubric.label: Identifies duplicates with ROW_NUMBER / GROUP BY
Keeps one row (MIN/MAX id or rn = 1)
Prevent recurrence with a unique constraint

s5.base: Write SQL to find consecutive login dates for a user.

rubric.label: Partitions by user and orders by date

s6.base: Review an AI-generated function that returns the wrong maximum value and identify the likely defect.

rubric.label: Bad initialisation (0 instead of first element / -inf)
Negative numbers / empty input edge cases

s6.base: Create a prompt that asks an AI tool to explain a legacy function without changing its behavior.

rubric.label: Explicit constraint: do not modify behaviour/code
Asks about side effects and edge cases

s6.base: Explain how you would verify an AI-generated solution before committing it.
Given an off-by-one loop bug, describe a systematic debugging process.

rubric.label: Reproduce with a minimal failing case
Fix and add a regression test

s6.base: Ask an AI assistant to generate unit tests for a string parser and define the required edge cases.

rubric.label: Names the test framework and structure

s6.base: Explain how to detect hallucinated APIs in AI-generated code.
Review an AI-generated SQL query for injection risks.

rubric.label: Spots string concatenation of user input

s6.base: Describe how you would compare AI-generated code with project coding standards.
Create a debugging checklist for code that works locally but fails in production.
Explain why generated code should be tested with boundary, negative, and adversarial inputs.

rubric.label: Generated code optimises for the happy path

s6.base: Design a prompt for refactoring duplicated code while preserving public interfaces.

rubric.label: Require tests to prove behaviour is preserved
Ask for a diff and explanation

s6.base: Explain how to use logs, stack traces, and minimal reproducible examples with an AI assistant.

rubric.label: Share the full stack trace / error

s6.base: Identify risks of blindly accepting generated dependency versions.
Describe how to ask an AI assistant for multiple algorithmic approaches and complexity analysis.

rubric.label: State the problem and constraints (input sizes)

s6.base: Explain how to validate generated authentication or authorization logic.

s7.base: Explain the request-response lifecycle in a web application.

rubric.label: Server routing, middleware and business logic
Response with status code and rendering

s7.base: Compare GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, and DELETE.
Differentiate cookies, sessions, local storage, and tokens.

rubric.label: Server-side sessions keyed by an id
localStorage is JS-accessible, not sent automatically

s7.base: Explain CORS and why browsers enforce it.

rubric.label: Why: protect users from malicious sites

s7.base: Design an API endpoint for creating and retrieving orders.
Explain JWT structure and common security risks.
Describe pagination, filtering, sorting, and rate limiting in APIs.
Explain webhooks and polling with use cases.

rubric.label: Webhooks: server pushes events via callbacks

s7.base: Compare server-side rendering and client-side rendering.

rubric.label: SSR renders HTML on the server
CSR renders in the browser with JS

s7.base: Explain CSRF, XSS, SQL injection, and mitigation strategies.

rubric.label: CSRF: forged requests using the victim's cookies

s7.base: Design a versioning strategy for a public API.

rubric.label: URI vs header vs query versioning

s7.base: Explain how to make an API observable and debuggable.

rubric.label: Meaningful error responses and health checks

s8.base: Design a parking-lot system using suitable classes and relationships.

rubric.label: Core classes (ParkingLot, Level, Spot, Vehicle, Ticket)
Vehicle/spot types via inheritance or enums
Error cases (out of stock, insufficient money)
Entities: Movie, Theatre, Screen, Show, Seat, Booking
Seat locking / holds to prevent double booking

Compare composition and inheritance in a design.
Design a notification system supporting email, SMS, and push.

Design a chess game at a high level.
Explain the Factory, Strategy, Observer, and Singleton patterns.

rubric.label: Search by capacity, time and amenities

s8.base: Explain how to make a class immutable.

rubric.label: Final/readonly fields set in the constructor

s8.base: Refactor a tightly coupled design using dependency injection.

s9.base: Explain horizontal scaling, vertical scaling, and auto-scaling.

rubric.label: Stateless services / load balancing enable scale-out

s9.base: Compare SQL and NoSQL for a high-volume application.

s9.base: Explain message queues, retries, and dead-letter queues.

s9.base: Explain consistency, availability, partition tolerance, and trade-offs.

s10.base: Compare unit, integration, system, regression, smoke, and sanity testing.

s10.base: Explain the software development life cycle.

s10.base: Write acceptance criteria for a password-reset feature.

rubric.label: Security: no user enumeration, rate limit

s10.base: Explain semantic versioning and release management.
Compare infrastructure as code and manual provisioning.

rubric.label: IaC defines infrastructure in versioned code
Review, testing and automation of changes

s10.base: Describe backup, rollback, and disaster-recovery planning.
